verdicts.claim: Checkpoint weight sizes: official BF16 4 shards 18,819,720,848 B (17.53 GiB); cyankiwi AWQ 8,991,501,696 B (8.37 GiB); ggml-org Q8_0 9,527,498,048 B (8.87 GiB) + mmproj Q8_0 624,229,728 B; bartowski Q8_0 9.55 GB, Q6_K_L 8.11 GB, Q4_K_M 5.84 GB, bf16 17.92 GB, mmproj bf16 0.92 GB, ~956k downloads

Architecture: Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration, 32 layers, 8 full_attention (every 4th), 4 KV heads, head_dim 256, GDN 16 key / 32 value heads dim 128, conv kernel 4, mamba_ssm_dtype float32, max_position_embeddings 262144, vision depth 27 width 1152, mtp_num_hidden_layers 1

vLLM KV math: 32,768 B/token BF16, 16,384 B/token FP8; GDN state about 49 MiB/seq; AWQ with vision pool 14.65-8.37-1.2 = 5.08 GiB -> 166k BF16 tokens, FP8 capped at 262,144; --language-model-only about 5.93 GiB -> 194k BF16
verdicts.correction: Arithmetic reproduces (5.08 GiB / 32768 B = 166,460 tokens). Caveat: vLLM pins one uniform page size across attention and GDN groups for hybrids (open #37121, RFC #55196), so FP8 KV gives about 2x only at long single-request context and little at short context; and the Qwen3.5 family never loads checkpoint KV scales (open #54623), so FP8 KV runs uncalibrated at scale 1.0. Prefer BF16 KV at --max-model-len 131072, which already fits with margin.

summary: I could not refute the record's runtime claims, and it holds with corrections. I checked all of this live on 2026-11-15: weight sizes from the HF API, config.json, vLLM v0.33.0 source (registry, both mimo parsers, the Rust MiMo parser, the recipe, CMakeLists), llama.cpp b12418 source and issues #29319/#29257, the GGUF templates through the HF gguf metadata API, and the Ollama tags page. Memory feasibility is solid. On vLLM, the cyankiwi AWQ checkpoint (8.37 GiB) leaves a 5.08 GiB KV pool, or about 5.93 GiB with --language-model-only, which gives 166k to 194k tokens with BF16 KV. In llama.cpp, Q8_0 with q8_0 KV at 262k needs about 14.2 GiB: KV is 17,408 B/token, not 16 KiB. Corrections: (1) Marlin on sm_120 is source-backed, since CMakeLists.txt:658 builds 12.0f. (2) FP8 KV gives about 2x only at long context on vLLM hybrids because of page pinning (#37121, #55196), and it runs uncalibrated because Qwen3.5 does not load KV scales (#54623). Prefer BF16 KV at 131072. (3) The ggml-org patched template says the model's native tool-call arguments are JSON, but the vLLM mimo parser expects <parameter> XML, so whether tool calls work in vLLM is contested and needs an end-to-end test with OpenCode. (4) The llama.cpp docker command does not persist its -hf cache. (5) The speed bounds are slightly too low because the embedding is not read in full per token. Gaps: no end-to-end tool-call test on either runtime, no measured tok/s, and no check that FA works with q8_0 KV at head_dim 256 on CUDA.
